From: Logan Pierce <logan@marketly.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation: Q4 price hold + commit uplift

Ava / Ben / Monica,

Thanks for the initial renewal worksheet. Marketly is very interested in expanding next year but we need two things to be comfortable committing: a short-term price hold through Q4 (to avoid the recent public cloud pricing blips) and a soft floor on committed units while we ramp usage. We also want the option to phase in a higher commit if usage warrants it — ideally with predictable step-up pricing.

Can Redwood propose a path that balances our need for predictability + your need for committed revenue? Also, we will need to see any SLA language that changes with the commit. I cc'd contracts@marketly.com for redlines.

Attached: Marketly_requested_terms.xlsx (placeholder)

—Logan

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Logan Pierce <logan@marketly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: Q4 price hold + commit uplift

Logan — thanks for the clear ask. We had a quick internal sync and here is a pragmatic path that should meet Marketly's ramp while keeping unit economics reasonable for both sides. High level:

- Short-term price hold: 6-week firm price hold through the end of Q4 on existing unit price for current SKUs.
- Soft floor: instead of a hard minimum commit, we propose a phased commit structure: an initial 3-month anchor commit at 60% of your expected run-rate, followed by two 3-month step-ups (80% then 100%) tied to simple usage gates.
- One-time onboarding credit: $50k credit applied at start of the renewal to offset migration and integration testing costs.
- Tiered uplift pricing: step-up pricing for the two uplift windows (we include a pricing matrix). If usage shoots past the step gate early, higher commit pricing is applied retroactively for that period.
- SLA/terms: no SLA reduction. We agreed to carve out a short exception window for scheduled maintenance during the first step-up month; full SLA otherwise.

I've attached a draft pricing matrix (2027-05-27_Marketly_PRICING_MATRIX.xlsx) and a summary term sheet. If that looks reasonable, can we get a meeting tomorrow to walk the math with finance and legal? Proposed times: 10:30am or 3:00pm PT.

Best,

Logan / Marketly Legal — appreciate the quick review and clear asks. Short answers and next steps: 

- Step-down on step-ups: we can adjust the step-up amounts down by 10 percentage points on the two uplift windows. That meets your desire for looser ramp while keeping us aligned on minimum economics.
- Retroactive cap: we can limit retroactive price application to a single billing cycle (as asked).
- SLA summary: attached one-pager (see link above) that preserves current SLA levels; the only operational change is the temporary maintenance carve-out during the first step-up month.
- Final commercial concession: Redwood will apply a one-time onboarding credit of $50k and extend the price hold for an additional 2 weeks if Marketly signs the renewal within 10 business days.

Next steps: Ava, can you lock in a 30-minute call with Marketly for Monday to sign off? We will prepare a redline of the order form and a DocuSign envelope once legal confirms.
